The representation of complex relationships is an important modeling task, and the object-oriented data model is a natural vehicle for this task.

(a) current object-oriented data models are inadequate for modeling relationships, and (b) an object-oriented database management system that supports the modeling of relationships must support: (i) the representation of relationships as first-class entities; (ii) the specification of the semantics of relationships; (iii) the specification of constraints on relationships; (iv) the manipulation of relationships; and (v) the manipulation of the semantics of the relationships.

In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a data model and query language to support modeling of relationships in object-oriented databases.
the development of a data model for the specification and manipulation of relationships among objects in an object-oriented database.
the development of a new object-oriented database model and its implementation on a commercial object-oriented database system, ONTOS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
object-oriented data modeling is a powerful tool for the representation and manipulation of complex relationships among the objects of the real world.
object-oriented data models are a good starting point for modeling complex relationships.
object-oriented databases have not been successful in the marketplace, and that they are likely to remain a research topic for a long time to come.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
object-oriented databases have a long way to go before they can support the modeling and management of complex relationships in the way relational systems do today.
we have shown that it is possible to model complex relationships among entities, and to query and update such models in an object-oriented environment.
the object-oriented approach is a promising paradigm for modeling complex relationships among objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the object-oriented data model can be extended to provide better support for modeling complex relationships among entities.
the modeling of relationships in object-oriented databases is not a trivial extension of the modeling of objects.
a more comprehensive object-oriented data model is needed.
